subject: Re: Pricing & capacity plan for inference-efficiency pilot
messages:
From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@valoracorp.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Rao <rajesh.rao@valoracorp.com>, procurement@valora.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing & capacity plan for inference-efficiency pilot

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Valora is interested in a 6-week pilot of Redwood's efficiency toolkit focused on reducing token cost for our conversational routing use case. High level: ~500K tokens/day currently, expected to grow to 1.5M in 3 months. Key asks:

- A pricing envelope for a pilot (credits, overage rates) that includes batching/caching settings you recommend for our workload.
- Quantization guidance: if we move to 4-bit int8-style quant (you mentioned multiple profiles), what accuracy delta should we expect for our NLU slot extraction?
- Any recommended guardrails or rollback steps if latency increases under real traffic.

Attached is a short doc with request details and an export of sample request size distribution. We need an internal finance check by 6/25.

Best,
Emily
Emily Turner
Head of Platform Integrations
Valora Health

Attachments: Valora_Efficiency_Pilot_Reqs.pdf
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@valoracorp.com>
Cc: Rajesh Rao <rajesh.rao@valoracorp.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & capacity plan for inference-efficiency pilot

Hi Emily — really appreciate the clear ask and the sample export. Quick summary and proposed next steps: 

1) Pilot pricing proposal (high level)
   - 6-week pilot: $18k flat credit pool + standard hosted per-token overage at 75% of published rate.
   - If Valora commits to a 6-month paid volume after pilot (tiered commit), we can convert pilot spend and apply a 12% one-time commit credit.

2) Batching & caching guidance (initial)
   - For conversational routing (many short requests) we recommend continuous micro-batching with max latency SLO 120ms and a target batch window of 20ms to capture burst benefits.
   - Prefix/KV caching in the router for repeated context (we can seed top-10 intents). Expect 25–35% token reduction based on similar customers.

3) Quantization recommendation
   - Start with our 8-bit quant profile (lowest risk) for the pilot; run a small A/B on 4-bit for non-critical routes. Typical slot extraction accuracy drop is <1.5% with our Q4 profile on similar models, but this is model-and-prompt dependent.

4) Rollback & guardrails
   - Canary 10% traffic on quantized variant, automatic fallback for p99 latency > 200ms or a quality-regression alert tied to a small sentinel prompt set.

I'll loop in Ben (runtime) and Lauren (pricing) to validate numbers and confirm if we can offer any additional pilot concessions. Do you have a preferred start date (week of 6/29 or 7/6)?

—Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Emily — copying Marissa from commercial strategy. Two tactical items from finance/ops: 

- We can reduce the pilot flat credit to $15k if Valora agrees to a short statement of intent to evaluate a 6-month commit (non-binding). That gives you more runway for experiments while keeping the pilot focused.

- Overage rate during pilot can be capped at a known uplift (we propose 60% of published rate) to give procurement certainty.

If acceptable, we'll prepare a short pilot SOW and a one-page mutual action plan. Sean — please confirm if we can commit to the 20ms batch window recommendation operationally for hosted customers and whether any additional infra reservation is needed.

Thanks,

Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Turner <emily.turner@valoracorp.com>, Rajesh Rao <rajesh.rao@valoracorp.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 14:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & capacity plan for inference-efficiency pilot

Emily / team — quick technical clarifications and our recommended pilot config (attaching a simple savings sim).

- Batch window: 20ms target is feasible on Redwood hosted for this volume profile; we'll configure continuous batching with adaptive backoff so tail latency stays within your 120ms SLO. No dedicated capacity required for the pilot.

- Caching: we'll implement a lightweight KV cache for user conversation prefixes and intent canonicalizations. For 500K tokens/day, expect an operational cache hit rate of ~18–28% in week 1, rising to 30–38% after heuristics/enz adjustments.

- Quantization profiles:
   * Q8-safe: 8-bit symmetric quant — negligible accuracy impact, minimal perf gain (~1.1x cost reduction).
   * Q4-balanced: our 4-bit profile with mixed-float layers for sensitive heads — typical accuracy delta 0.6–2.0% depending on prompt; cost reduction ~2.0–2.8x.
   * Q4-aggressive: higher throughput, risk of mild degradation on low-support slots (2–4% delta). Use only for batch-processed summarization routes.

- Suggested pilot cadence: week 1 baseline (no quant), week 2 Q8 A/B, week 3 Q4-balanced canary 10–20% with sentinel evaluation, weeks 4–6 scale chosen profile and tune batching windows.

- Guardrails & rollback: automated circuit that flips traffic to baseline model if quality regression threshold exceeded or if p99 latency crosses 200ms for more than two 5-minute intervals. We'll supply a small test harness and 20 sentinel prompts to run nightly checks.

Attaching: valora-savings-sim.xlsx (simple token-cost model across batch/cache/quant knobs).

Happy to walk through the sim with your infra/ML team on a quick call. Proposed SOW draft link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cValoraProposal

—Ben
Principal Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
